name: Strait of Hormuz
note: Roughly a fifth of the world's oil supply passes through here.
description: The Strait of Hormuz is the world's most consequential oil chokepoint. Every tanker leaving the Persian Gulf — from the terminals of Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Kuwait, Qatar, and Iran — must round the Musandam Peninsula through this single passage into the Gulf of Oman. Roughly a fifth of the world's petroleum passes through waters about thirty-nine kilometres wide at their narrowest, in shipping lanes narrower still. The strait's geography has made it a pressure gauge for the global economy: when tensions rise here, as they did during the Tanker War of the 1980s, markets everywhere feel it within hours.
